Publishing and exporting

The Publish view writes the sheet as a report. Figures, sweep charts and the states table can also be exported on their own, and the whole sheet can be written as a MATLAB script that uses the Dome toolbox.

The Publish view

The Publish tab in the header, or File › Export › Report, opens the Publish view: the options at the left and a preview of the report at the right. The preview changes with each option. The report always uses the sheet as written, never a value from a drag or the sweep slider.

FormatFile
PDFA PDF report, on Letter or A4 paper.
HTMLOne HTML file, with the equations and figures inside it.
LaTeXA zip file holding the .tex file and each figure as a PDF.
MATLAB scriptA .m file: the equations as MATLAB statements, then the figures chosen under Include.

Include chooses the parts of the report: the equations typeset, their values beside them, a table of inputs, the states table, comments as text, each figure, a sweep that has run, and the sheet source. The report's title is the first %% section of the sheet unless another is typed. The Author field is optional; when it is filled in, the report carries the name.

A comment at the end of a line belongs to that line. It is printed beside the line's equation, or, for an input shown in the table of inputs, in the table's Description column. A comment on a line of its own is a paragraph where it stands, and comment lines in a row make one paragraph. A %% heading with nothing printed under it, such as one over inputs that the table of inputs shows, is left out. The names in Dome's own text, such as the heading of a sweep, a caption or an axis title, are set as in the equations: T_3 is T with subscript 3, eta is η. Comments are printed as typed. A character that the PDF's fonts or LaTeX lack is set as in the equations, so Ẇ is a W with a dot over it, and a character with no TeX equivalent, such as ⌘, is printed in DejaVu Serif. The table of inputs gives each input in the unit it was typed in, so m_a = 100 [lb/min] is 100 lb/min. A heading stays on the page with what follows it. With the sheet source included, a report with a sweep also gives the sweep's lines, so that the sweep can be run again from the report.

The MATLAB script

With MATLAB script chosen, the options for the written report are turned off, the figures can still be chosen, and one option is added: States from the Dome MATLAB toolbox. Checked (the default), the script computes each state with the toolbox, so it computes again when an input in the script changes. Unchecked, the states are written into the script as numbers, and the script runs without the toolbox. The same script, with the option as set here, is File › Export › MATLAB script. The script carries the sheet's comments: a comment at the end of a line ends the script's line for that statement, and comment lines stand above the statement they stood above in the sheet.

The File menu

  • New, Open, Save, Save as: sheets are .dome files. Open also reads a .txt or .m file of sheet lines into a new sheet.
  • Save as template: a copy of the sheet that opens as a new, unsaved sheet, as a starting point for others.
  • MATLAB script: the sheet as a .m file, as in the Publish view.
  • States table: the states table as a .csv file, for a spreadsheet.
  • Report: the Publish view.

Figures

The export button in a figure's header writes the figure as it is shown, with its zoom and display options:

  • PNG at 300 dpi, SVG and PDF as vector drawings for reports.
  • Copy image puts the figure on the clipboard.
  • Copy data copies the states of the figure as tab-separated text.
  • MATLAB script writes a script that draws the same diagram in MATLAB.

Sweep charts have the same menu, with CSV added (see Sweeps).
